dialogues.speaker: Faruzan
dialogues.text: Oh, you're back. Ready to delve into the art of solving mechanical puzzles? Or, did you want to have a chat?

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: I like the enthusiasm. I can see a thirst for knowledge shining in your eyes, so let's see what you've got!

choices.text: I wanted to ask a few questions, actually.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Hmph, as you wish. When it's you doing the asking, I'm an open book.

choices.text: Would you prefer a doll that is cute or refined?

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Not that I have anything against "cuteness." A plush little thing with big eyes and a round face... I can see the appeal as much as anyone.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: But at my age, clinging to such objects like a child is somewhat... undignified.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Now, some of the newer stuff on the market is just exquisite... made with the finest material, sculpted in elegant lines, with features that glitter like gemstones...

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: The element of cuteness is there. But, it also doubles as a piece of art...

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Wait a second... I thought your questions were going to be academic in nature. What is the meaning of this?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just... wanted to learn more about you!

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Ahem! Fine. I'll let it go this once. But, that excuse won't work a second time!

choices.text: Which is better... Autonomous or manually-operated devices?

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: I don't think this is a question that has a definitive answer... not for me, at least. It depends entirely on the scenario.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Simply put, if the task requires repetitive mechanical work that dilutes the value of human mental labor, then automated devices are superior.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: But where "identification," "analysis," and "decision-making" are critical, manual control is always safer.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Human thought is complex. Even if we were to simulate a six-year-old's mind, the demands in terms of component design, system weight, and energy cost would be immense.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: As I see it, conventional hardware capable of simulating adult-level cognition is impossible to integrate into a compact device — for the foreseeable future, anyway.

choices.text: That was a very concise summary.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Well, I've told you before, if you find these topics interesting, you should come to my classes.

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Cyrus's student, Lisa Minci, is known as a "once in a generation" genius. But, with your smarts, I bet you could give her a run for her Mora!

choices.text: I've got a few other things to wrap up...

response.speaker: Faruzan
response.text: Of course! Don't let me keep you. Come back whenever you're ready.
